---
title: "SPEC-4.2.1-v001"
subtitle: "Preview fidelity: CSSOM styles captured; manual refresh"
---

## Problem

Previews of some sites (e.g. openstax.org) rendered as a nearly unstyled
page dominated by giant SVG icons, and re-selecting the tab appeared not
to help.

Two causes:

1. **Lost styles, not staleness.** The capture used
   `document.documentElement.outerHTML`, which serializes only text that
   sits *inside* tags. CSS-in-JS libraries (styled-components / emotion in
   production) leave their `<style>` tags empty and insert every rule
   directly into the CSSOM via `insertRule` — so the capture dropped most
   of such a page's styling. Every re-capture produced the same broken
   render, which looked like a frozen preview.
2. There was no way to force a re-capture of the currently previewed tab
   after the live page changed (e.g. dismissing a full-screen dialog) —
   only selecting a different tab and back would refetch.

## Fix

- `tabService.getTabContent` now serializes CSSOM rules into an extra
  `<style data-tabmaster-cssom>` block appended to `</head>`:
  - `<style>` sheets whose owner tag is **empty** (the CSS-in-JS case) —
    sheets whose text already serializes via outerHTML are skipped to
    avoid duplication, as are `<link>` sheets (they reload through the
    injected `<base href>`);
  - `document.adoptedStyleSheets` (constructable stylesheets);
  - cross-origin sheets are skipped (unreadable); output is capped at
    600 KB per capture; `</style` inside rule text is escaped.
  - Card-view thumbnails share this capture path and gain the same
    fidelity.
- The preview panel header gained a **refresh button** (circular arrow,
  next to "Switch to actual tab") that re-captures the current tab on
  demand; it spins while the capture is in flight.

## Version

`package.json` / `manifest.json` bumped **4.2.0 → 4.2.1**.
